title: Data Integration and Interoperability
html:
1Definition and Goals

Definition: Processes related to the movement and consolidation of data within and between data stores, applications, and organizations.

Interoperability: Ability of multiple systems to communicate with each other.

Integration: Consolidates data in one place; resolves data inconsistencies; converts data to common formats.

3 Goals:

  1. Make data available in the format and timeframe needed by data consumers and business applications
  2. Lower cost and complexity of managing solutions by developing shared models and interfaces
  3. Ensure critical data is available where needed, when needed — securely and reliably

2Business Drivers

  • Accessing data from multiple systems and sources
  • Reducing the cost of data movement and conversion
  • Adhering to regulatory requirements
  • Aligning data with business needs
  • Providing accurate and timely information for business decisions
  • Supporting migration from legacy systems
  • Enabling Master Data Management

3Three Guiding Principles

  1. Design for re-use — approaches and solutions designed for maximum reuse; transformation code and mappings remain stable as source/target systems change
  2. Abstraction — abstract interface from implementation; allows multiple sources/targets to interact with single interface
  3. Shared responsibility — DII requires cooperation between technical and business teams; business stewards validate transformation rules; technical teams implement

4Essential Concepts

Latency

The time delay between when data is produced and when it is available for consumption.

6 Latency Types (from most to least delay):

Type Description
Batch Data moved in bulk at scheduled intervals (hours to days); most latency
Change Data Capture (CDC) Only changed data is moved; less overhead than full batch
Near-Real-Time Data available within seconds to minutes of source change
Asynchronous Data moved without waiting for response; may have some delay
Synchronous Immediate; calling system waits for response before proceeding
Streaming Continuous flow; lowest latency
Exam tip

Batch = highest latency; Streaming = lowest latency

Transformation

Data is transformed to reconcile differences in data representations:

  • Structural — converting formats (e.g., XML to relational)
  • Semantic — reconciling different meanings of same concept across systems
  • Calculated / Derived — applying business rules to calculate new values

ETL vs. ELT:

  • ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) — transformation occurs before loading; traditional approach
  • ELT (Extract, Load, Transform) — data loaded first then transformed in target; used in Big Data/data lake environments

Interaction Models (3 Types)

Model Description
Point-to-Point Direct connections between systems; simple but becomes complex as systems scale (n*(n-1)/2 interfaces for n systems)
Hub-and-Spoke Central hub receives and routes data; reduces connections; hub is single point of failure
Publish-Subscribe Publishers send data to topics; subscribers receive relevant data; loose coupling

Interface Formula: For point-to-point with n systems: n × (n-1) / 2 unique interfaces

Architecture Patterns

Enterprise Service Bus (ESB):

  • Middleware layer coordinating messaging between services
  • Provides routing, transformation, protocol translation
  • Component of Service-Oriented Architecture (SOA)

SOA (Service-Oriented Architecture):

  • Architecture where services are loosely coupled, interoperable, reusable
  • Enables sharing of business functions across systems
  • Services exposed via standard interfaces (e.g., web services)

Complex Event Processing (CEP):

  • Processes multiple events in real time
  • Identifies patterns and triggers responses
  • Used for real-time analytics (e.g., fraud detection)

DaaS (Data-as-a-Service):

  • Data provided via web service on demand
  • Data management isolated from data consumers

5Data Integration Tools and Approaches

ETL Tools

  • Automate extraction from sources, applying transformations, loading to target
  • Generate technical Metadata (lineage)
  • Provide audit and logging capabilities

ELT (vs. ETL)

  • Load raw data first; transform within target system
  • Common in Hadoop/data lake environments
  • Target system must have processing capacity

Data Federation / Virtualization

  • Provides unified view of data without physically moving it
  • Real-time access to distributed sources
  • No persistent copies

Replication

  • Copies of data maintained in multiple locations
  • Used for performance, availability, disaster recovery

Data Services (Web Services)

  • Expose data operations via standard interfaces
  • SOAP or REST protocols
  • Enable system-agnostic data access

6Data Exchange Standards

NIEM (National Information Exchange Model)

  • US Federal data exchange standard
  • Framework and methodology for developing data exchanges between organizations
  • Supports consistent data sharing across government agencies
  • Key: NIEM is a standard and methodology, NOT a technology

Canonical Model

  • Definition: A common, enterprise-wide data model used as a standard for data exchange
  • Reduces transformation complexity
  • Instead of N×(N-1) point-to-point mappings, systems map to/from canonical model
  • Also called: canonical data model, common data model

XML and JSON

  • XML — widely used for data exchange; supports structured and semi-structured data
  • JSON — lightweight, preferred for web services and NoSQL environments

7Data Integration Architecture Components

Data Hubs and Shared Storage

  • Operational Data Store (ODS) — integration point for operational systems; current, near-real-time data
  • Data Warehouse — integrated, historical, subject-oriented data for analysis
  • Data Lake — stores raw data in native format; schema applied at read time

Interaction Points

  • APIs (Application Programming Interfaces) — define how systems interact
  • Web Services — expose functionality over HTTP; SOAP or REST
  • Message Queues — hold messages between systems; enables asynchronous communication

8Activities

Activity 1: Define Data Integration and Interoperability Architecture

  • Assess current state; define target architecture
  • Select appropriate interaction models (point-to-point, hub-and-spoke, publish-subscribe)
  • Define data exchange standards and canonical models

Activity 2: Design Data Integration Solutions

  • Capture source-to-target mapping requirements
  • Define transformation rules
  • Establish error handling and logging requirements

Activity 3: Develop Data Integration Solutions

  • Implement ETL/ELT processes
  • Build and test data services
  • Document data lineage

Activity 4: Implement Data Flows

  • Deploy and schedule integration processes
  • Monitor data flows and performance
  • Handle exceptions and data quality issues

Activity 5: Maintain and Monitor Data Integration Solutions

  • Monitor latency, throughput, error rates
  • Manage changes to source/target schemas
  • Tune performance

9Interaction Model Comparison

Aspect Point-to-Point Hub-and-Spoke Publish-Subscribe
Connections n(n-1)/2 n×2 (to/from hub) Via topics/queues
Complexity High as n grows Managed centrally Loose coupling
Single Point of Failure No Yes (hub) Depends on implementation
Latency Low Moderate Low to moderate
Best For Few systems, simple Many systems, centralized Event-driven, many consumers

10Governance and Metrics

Key Governance Concerns:

  • Data lineage — tracking data from source to target
  • Transformation rule management — ensuring business rules documented and approved
  • Error handling standards — consistent approach to failed integrations
  • Metadata management — source-to-target mappings, technical lineage

Metrics:

  • Latency: actual vs. target delivery time
  • Data quality: error rates in integration processes
  • Availability: percentage of time integration services are operational
  • Volume: records processed per unit time
  • Rejects: number of records failing validation

11Practice Q&A

Q1: What is the definition of Data Integration and Interoperability? A: Processes related to the movement and consolidation of data within and between data stores, applications, and organizations.

Q2: What is the formula for the number of interfaces in a point-to-point architecture with n systems? A: n × (n-1) / 2.

Q3: What are the 6 latency types from most to least latency? A: Batch, CDC, Near-Real-Time, Asynchronous, Synchronous, Streaming.

Q4: What is the difference between ETL and ELT? A: ETL transforms data before loading into target; ELT loads raw data first, then transforms within the target system (common in Big Data/data lake environments).

Q5: What are the 3 interaction models? A: Point-to-Point, Hub-and-Spoke, Publish-Subscribe.

Q6: What is an ESB? A: Enterprise Service Bus — middleware coordinating messaging between services; provides routing, transformation, protocol translation; component of SOA.

Q7: What is SOA? A: Service-Oriented Architecture — architecture where services are loosely coupled, interoperable, and reusable; services exposed via standard interfaces.

Q8: What is a Canonical Model? A: A common, enterprise-wide data model used as a standard for data exchange; reduces transformation complexity instead of point-to-point mappings.

Q9: What is NIEM? A: National Information Exchange Model — US Federal framework and methodology for data exchanges between organizations; standard, not technology.

Q10: What is CEP? A: Complex Event Processing — processes multiple events in real time to identify patterns and trigger responses (e.g., fraud detection).

Q11: What are the 3 guiding principles of DII? A: Design for re-use, Abstraction, Shared responsibility.

Q12: What is DaaS? A: Data-as-a-Service — data provided via web service on demand; data management isolated from consumers.

Q13: What is the key advantage of hub-and-spoke over point-to-point? A: Reduces the number of connections managed; centralizes transformation and routing at the hub (though the hub becomes a single point of failure).

Q14: What is data federation/virtualization? A: Providing a unified view of data without physically moving it; real-time access to distributed sources; no persistent copies.

Q15: What is publish-subscribe architecture? A: Publishers send data to topics; subscribers receive data they are interested in; loose coupling between systems.

12Quick Reference

3 Goals Available in format/time needed; lower cost; critical data secure and reliable
3 Guiding Principles Re-use, Abstraction, Shared responsibility

Latency (most to least) Batch → CDC → Near-Real-Time → Async → Sync → Streaming
ETL Transform before load
ELT Load then transform (Big Data/data lake)
ESB Enterprise Service Bus — middleware for service coordination
SOA Service-Oriented Architecture — loosely coupled services
CEP Complex Event Processing — real-time event pattern detection
NIEM US Federal data exchange standard and methodology
Canonical Model Enterprise-wide common model reducing transformation complexity
DaaS Data-as-a-Service — data via web service on demand
Hub single point of failure Hub-and-Spoke architecture risk
